headline: Bitcoin is holding in the mid-$64,000s with fear still extreme, as the Fed's October minutes land overnight Bangkok time and Anthropic's giant share sale is set to price above its range.

market.asOf: Read at about 11:55-11:58 UTC Wed 18 Nov (about 18:55 Bangkok): BTC $64,220 (down 1.09% in 24 hours) on CoinLore, $64,198.95 (down 1.15%) on Binance.US; ETH $1,800 (down 1.10%) on CoinLore; SOL $74.38 (up 2.30%) on CoinGecko. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear: alternative.me's Crypto Fear & Greed Index 12 (10 yesterday, 32 a week ago, 53 a month ago), read at about 11:55 UTC Wed 18 Nov.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds in the mid-$64,000s in 'extreme fear' as fund outflows and a likely Fed rate rise weigh
stories.summary: Bitcoin is still stuck in the range it has held since 15 November while traders wait for minutes of the Fed's October meeting, out tonight Bangkok time. US bitcoin funds lost money on Tuesday, stablecoin balances are shrinking, and markets see a December rate rise as close to certain.
points: Bitcoin was back in 'its $64,000-$66,000 range' it has held since 15 Nov, above Sunday's 18-week low of $62,000, per Cryptonews at 11:43 UTC Wednesday.
US spot bitcoin ETFs had net outflows of $239.94 million on Tuesday 17 Nov, led by BlackRock's IBIT at $209.54 million; spot ether ETFs lost $29.1 million, per Farside data reported by FinanceFeeds.
CME FedWatch showed a 95.7% chance of a 0.25-point December rate rise and 4.3% for a 0.5-point rise, per FinanceFeeds. These are market bets, not a Fed decision.
Total stablecoin supply fell 5.3% in 30 days to $284.24 billion, the steepest drop since Terra in 2022, per CoinDesk. Less stablecoin money usually means less fresh buying power for crypto.
Minutes of the Fed's 27-28 October meeting are due at 2:00pm ET Wednesday (02:00 Thursday Bangkok), per the Federal Reserve's calendar.

sources.label: FinanceFeeds: bitcoin, Nvidia and Fed minutes

stories.title: Anthropic's giant share sale is set to price above its range tonight, with Nasdaq trading as ANT on Thursday
stories.summary: AI company Anthropic is due to set the price of its first public share sale on Wednesday, and reports say strong demand could push it above the top of its $70-78 range. Its shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday.
points: The Wall Street Journal reports Anthropic expects to price above $80 a share, which would value it at about $1.5-1.6 trillion, per Yahoo Finance.
The offer is 825 million shares plus a $26 billion private placement with Google, Amazon and Nvidia; up to 20% of the shares may go to individual investors, per Yahoo Finance.
At $78 a share the deal would raise about $90.4 billion including the placement, and orders came in about 7 times the shares on offer, per Seoul Economic Daily.

Shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq as ANT on Thursday 19 Nov. Seoul Economic Daily says trading starts at 9:30am ET (21:30 Bangkok); StockTitan says Nasdaq opens a new listing only when the lead bank is ready, so the first trade may come later.

sources.label: Yahoo Finance: Anthropic eyes price above range

stories.title: Nvidia beats forecasts and raises its outlook, but says Jensen Huang will not return as CEO
stories.summary: Nvidia's sales came in well above forecasts and it guided higher, lifting its shares before the US open. But its board ruled out bringing back Jensen Huang, and the Wall Street Journal reports an SEC investigation.
points: Quarterly revenue was $115.84 billion, up 103.2%, against $108.85 billion expected; adjusted earnings were $2.68 a share against $2.47, per Investing.com.
Nvidia guided next-quarter revenue to $130 billion, per Investing.com.
Chairman Harvey Jones said the board 'does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO'; Colette Kress is interim CEO and stays CFO, per Yahoo Finance.
The Wall Street Journal reports an SEC civil investigation; the SEC declined to comment, per Yahoo Finance.
Shares were up about 3% before the open and Nasdaq 100 futures were up 1%, per Cryptonews.

briefs.title: DBS and Circle open 24/7 USDC minting in Asia
briefs.summary: Eligible DBS institutional clients can now swap dollars for USDC and back at any hour, per The Block.

briefs.title: Etherscan warns of phishing after support-desk break-in attempt
briefs.summary: Someone tried to break into Etherscan's support ticket system; it has not said whether data was exposed and says staff will never ask for a private key or seed phrase, per TokenPost.

briefs.title: Polygon weighs buying banking licenses
briefs.summary: Co-founder Sandeep Nailwal says Polygon plans to spend about $50M-$100M per acquisition on banking and payments licenses in several regions, per TokenPost.

briefs.title: XRP and other altcoin funds also saw outflows
briefs.summary: On 17 Nov, XRP ETFs lost $6.14M, Hyperliquid $1.53M and Chainlink $1.33M, per FinanceFeeds.

briefs.title: Judge clears the 'MEV brothers' in $25M Ethereum case
briefs.summary: US District Judge Jessica Clarke acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno of fraud and money-laundering conspiracy over an alleged $25M exploit of trading bots, ending the first US criminal case over MEV, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: CFTC orders Kalshi to halt Trump 'mention' markets
briefs.summary: The CFTC ordered Kalshi to stop listing contracts on what President Trump will say and opened proceedings; Kalshi says it is complying, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Coinbase crypto-backed loans now in all 50 US states
briefs.summary: New York was the last state added; users can borrow USDC against BTC, ETH or SOL, and the product has made over $3.4B in loans since January 2025, per The Block.

briefs.title: Solana Foundation takes majority stake in CoinGecko
briefs.summary: The price was not disclosed; the foundation plans to add Solana-powered trading to CoinGecko's site and app, which has 18M registered users, per CoinDesk.
